problem: A production release lineage was blocked by an expired Netlify MCP proxy credential (401). After credential recovery, Netlify later exposed an exact production deploy for protected main. A subsequent GitHub Production Release Readback run was cancelled by concurrency while browser verification was still executing, so provider deployment truth and functional terminal proof must remain distinct.
root_cause: Temporary Netlify MCP proxy credentials can expire independently of application code and must not be treated as durable deploy authority.
Production provider identity can become proven before a broader GitHub browser-readback workflow reaches a terminal conclusion.
Cancelling or superseding a readback workflow must not erase already observed immutable provider deploy evidence, but it also must not manufacture functional browser proof.
prevention: Classify Netlify 401 at the deploy transport as an auth incident before changing product code.
Persist immutable Netlify deploy evidence when state=ready, context=production and commit_ref is observed.
Treat provider exact-SHA proof and functional browser proof as separate gates; both are required when the obligation requires browser behavior.
A cancelled or superseded readback run may reuse already proven immutable provider identity, but skipped or cancelled functional checks must be resumed on the newest canonical lineage.
Never downgrade an already proven provider deployment merely because a later verifier is cancelled; never upgrade a cancelled verifier into LIVE_BEWEZEN without its required functional evidence.
Store root cause, prevention, provider evidence and recovery outcome in Brain before terminal closure.

completed_steps: Wait for exact live release marker and deploy identity
